metadata.name: Agent
metadata.purpose: WhatsApp-based customer service agent for TechRepair Polanco Service Center that handles repair order tracking, general support inquiries, warranty questions, pricing information, and delivery logistics for TechRepair device repairs in Mexico City
capabilities: Intent classification and routing (status checks, general support, warranty, pricing, delivery logistics, escalation)
Order status lookup and tracking via service order numbers
Multi-order disambiguation for customers with multiple active repairs
Warranty determination and guidance (in-warranty vs out-of-warranty)
Pricing information delivery with intake fees and repair cost quotations
Delivery logistics handling for both door-to-door (D2D) and carry-in service types
Customer memory extraction and persistence across conversations
Event detection (order received confirmations, address changes, payment receipts)
Escalation detection and handoff to human agents based on frustration signals or complex issues
Bilingual support (Spanish and English) with conversation history context
Contact information provision (service center hours, location, phone numbers)
Customer corrections handling for name and address updates
metadata.execution_variant: Runtime-level outcomes for executing against tech_repair-live-agent (:3098). Derived 2026-07-23 from tech_repair_whatsapp_map.json — keep that file pristine for research arms.

error_handling.malformed_response: verifyDetectedEvents validates event detection, parseCorrections and applyCorrections handle correction attempts
error_handling.tool_failure: assertNoHedgeWords validates response quality, fallback to escalation via shouldEscalate and escalationNode

guardrails: assertNoHedgeWords - prevents hedging language in responses
verifyDetectedEvents - validates keyword-detected events using LLM to avoid false positives from negations/sarcasm
shouldEscalate - checks if conversation requires human intervention
normalizeIntentForVersion - ensures intent compatibility across versions
EventDetector with two-stage validation (keyword then LLM verification)
Language detection and routing (joinSpanish for Spanish responses)
Memory extraction focuses only on persistent facts, explicitly ignoring emotions and temporary details
typical_flow: Extract memory from conversation history using memoryExtractionNode
Detect events in customer message using eventDetectorNode with keyword detection and LLM verification
Route message to appropriate handler using routerNode (classifies intent via ROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT)

Execute intent-specific node: statusNode (order status), supportNode (technical issues), pricingAnswerNode (pricing questions), warrantyAnswerNode (warranty inquiries), or contactInfoNode (contact info)
If escalation needed, route to escalationNode with buildHandoffContext
If human takeover detected, route to humanTakenOverNode
Format response through responseNode with truncateResponse and runSideEffects
Route conversation continuation using routeAfterSupport or routeByIntent
orchestrator.ambiguity_handling: multiOrderDisambiguation handles multiple order scenarios, routerNode uses ROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT rule 'If unsure, lean toward support_question', classifyByKeywords provides fast intent classification with classifyByLLM as fallback for complex cases, conversation history context passed to router for disambiguation

tools.name: lookupOrder
tools.description: Retrieves a service order record from the database by its order number
preconditions: svcOrderNo must be a valid string
postconditions: No state changes - read-only operation
side_effects: Executes database query against service_orders table

tools.name: routeByIntent
tools.description: Routes conversation flow from router node to appropriate handler based on detected user intent, handling escalation and human takeover scenarios
preconditions: state object must be valid WhatsAppStateType
intent must be classified in state
postconditions: No state changes - only returns routing decision

tools.name: routeAfterSupport
tools.description: Routes conversation flow after support node, directing to memory extraction on goodbye intent or directly to response for other intents
preconditions: state object must be valid WhatsAppStateType
postconditions: No state changes - only returns routing decision

tools.name: buildGraph
tools.description: Constructs and compiles the WhatsApp agent state graph with all nodes and routing edges
preconditions: all node functions must be defined
postconditions: Compiled graph is ready for execution

tools.name: getCheckpointer
tools.description: Initializes or retrieves the conversation state checkpointer, using PostgreSQL/Supabase for production or in-memory for development
preconditions: POSTGRES_CONNECTION_STRING must be configured in environment
postconditions: Checkpointer is initialized and ready for use
Database tables are set up if using PostgreSQL
side_effects: May create database tables via setup()

tools.name: getGraph
tools.description: Returns the compiled WhatsApp agent graph, building it on first call and caching for subsequent calls
postconditions: Graph is compiled and cached
Checkpointer is initialized

tools.name: planPricingResponse
tools.description: Determines appropriate pricing response strategy based on service order state, handling warranty status, payment pending, and escalation scenarios
preconditions: Service order data must be valid
Pricing state classification logic must be available
postconditions: No state changes - only returns response plan

tools.name: getCustomerInfo
tools.description: Extracts customer information from the assembled conversation context
preconditions: state object must be valid WhatsAppStateType
postconditions: No state changes - read-only accessor

tools.name: getActiveOrders
tools.description: Retrieves active service orders from context, sorted deterministically by order number (newest first) for consistent single-order selection
preconditions: state object must be valid WhatsAppStateType
postconditions: No state changes - returns sorted copy of orders

tools.name: getSessionInfo
tools.description: Extracts session information from the assembled conversation context
preconditions: state object must be valid WhatsAppStateType
postconditions: No state changes - read-only accessor

tools.name: shouldEscalate
tools.description: Determines if a conversation should be escalated to a human agent based on whether escalation attempts have exceeded a threshold
preconditions: state object must contain escalationAttempts property

tools.name: formatConversationHistory
tools.description: Formats recent conversation history into a human-readable string for prompt injection into LLM context
preconditions: state object must have context with conversation_history array

tools.name: createInitialState
tools.description: Initializes a new WhatsApp conversation state object with default values from assembled context and lane configuration
preconditions: context must be a valid AssembledContext object
postconditions: New state object is created with default values for conversation tracking

tools.name: makeSO
tools.description: Creates a service order object with default warranty and status values, allowing partial overrides

tools.name: stateWithOrders
tools.description: Creates a mock or test state object populated with provided service orders and default session/customer data
preconditions: orders array must contain objects with at least svc_order_no property

tools.name: contactInfoNode
tools.description: Retrieves and formats contact phone numbers (agent line for self-service and store line for human assistance) from dynamic configuration
preconditions: Contact numbers must be available in configuration

tools.name: parseCorrections
tools.description: Extracts and validates correction markers (format: [CORRECT:...]) from LLM response text to identify fields that need updating based on customer input
preconditions: CORRECT_MARKER_RE regex pattern must be defined

tools.name: applyCorrections
tools.description: Persists validated corrections to database by updating customer_memory fields and creating audit trail entries in interaction_history

parameters.name: args

preconditions: corrections must be validated ParsedCorrection objects
customer_memory record must exist for phone number
postconditions: customer_memory fields are updated with corrected values
interaction_history entries are created with source='human_correction' for audit trail

tools.name: deliveryLogisticsDispatchNode
tools.description: Routes delivery logistics handling based on service type, specifically differentiating carry-in orders from door-to-door delivery
preconditions: state must contain context with active orders

tools.name: isFirstOutbound
tools.description: Checks if this is the first outbound message from the assistant in the conversation by examining conversation history
preconditions: state must have context with conversation_history array

tools.name: styleCtx
tools.description: Creates a context object for styling WhatsApp messages with conversation metadata and intent information
preconditions: Valid WhatsApp state object must be provided
postconditions: Context object is created for message styling

tools.name: logThought
tools.description: Logs agent's internal reasoning/thoughts to a database for debugging and monitoring purposes
postconditions: Agent thought is persisted to database for conversation tracking
side_effects: Non-fatal error handling (catches and suppresses errors)

tools.name: eventDetectorNode
tools.description: Detects specific events or keywords in incoming messages using a two-stage approach (fast keyword detection, then AI verification)
preconditions: State must contain current_message with content and type
postconditions: Events/keywords are identified in the message

tools.name: memoryExtractionNode
tools.description: Extracts relevant information from conversation history to build context/memory for the agent
preconditions: Conversation history must not be empty
postconditions: Relevant memory/context is extracted from conversation transcript

tools.name: joinSpanish
tools.description: Formats an array of strings into a grammatically correct Spanish list with 'y' (and) conjunction
postconditions: Items are joined with proper Spanish grammar

tools.name: multiOrderDisambiguation
tools.description: Generates Spanish text to help customers disambiguate between multiple active service orders
postconditions: Disambiguation message is generated in Spanish

tools.name: intakeFeeCopy
tools.description: Generates Spanish text explaining the intake/diagnostic fee for a service order
postconditions: Fee explanation message is generated in Spanish

tools.name: quotedCopy
tools.description: Generates Spanish text presenting a repair quotation price to the customer
preconditions: Valid numeric total amount must be provided
postconditions: Quote message is generated in Spanish with formatted price

tools.name: pricingAnswerNode
tools.description: Handles customer inquiries about pricing by retrieving active orders and generating appropriate pricing responses
preconditions: Valid WhatsApp state with customer context
postconditions: Appropriate pricing response is generated based on order status

tools.name: runSideEffects
tools.description: Executes side effects like registering cost follow-ups based on specified effect types
preconditions: Supabase client available if phone provided
postconditions: Cost follow-up is registered in database if effect kind is register_cost_followup

tools.name: truncateResponse
tools.description: Truncates text to fit within WhatsApp's character limit, attempting to break at sentence boundaries (period or newline) when possible to maintain readability
preconditions: text and maxLength must be provided
postconditions: returned text length is <= maxLength

tools.name: buildEscalationResponse
tools.description: Generates customer-facing escalation message in Mexican Spanish (tuteo style) when bot transfers to human agent, optionally including order number for context
postconditions: customer receives escalation acknowledgment message

tools.name: resolveTypedReason
tools.description: Determines the escalation reason enum by checking for explicit override in state, or mapping from customer intent (frustration/complaint) to reason category
preconditions: state object must be valid WhatsAppStateType
postconditions: typed escalation reason is resolved for categorization

tools.name: buildHandoffContext
tools.description: Extracts and formats context data from conversation state for human agent handoff, including customer name, active orders, register type, and store contact line
preconditions: state contains customer and order data
postconditions: handoff context is prepared for human agent

tools.name: buildWaitTimeNotice
tools.description: Generates time-sensitive notice message in Spanish warning customer about session window closing, with urgency based on remaining minutes
postconditions: appropriate time warning message is generated

tools.name: responseNode
tools.description: Main response orchestrator that checks if conversation should escalate based on threshold, preserves existing handoff text, or generates appropriate bot response
postconditions: escalation decision is made and response is prepared

tools.name: escalationNode
tools.description: Marks conversation as escalated and generates customer-facing handoff message using priority logic: preserved responseText, typed reason with renderHandoff, or legacy generic bounce
postconditions: conversation is marked as escalated
escalation_reason is persisted to database/logs
customer receives handoff message
human agent queue is notified
side_effects: writes escalation status to conversation state

tools.name: humanTakenOverNode
tools.description: Marks that a human agent has assumed control of the conversation and sends confirmation message to customer in Spanish
postconditions: humanTakenOver flag is set
customer is notified of human takeover
bot stops responding automatically
side_effects: updates conversation state to disable bot auto-responses

tools.name: normalizeIntentForVersion
tools.description: Filters and maps intent values to ensure compatibility with specified taxonomy version (v1 or v2), converting legacy intents to modern equivalents
postconditions: returned intent is valid for requested taxonomy version

tools.name: classifyByKeywords
tools.description: Performs fast keyword-based intent classification using regex pattern matching against predefined keyword map, returning matched intent and confidence
postconditions: intent is classified if keywords match, otherwise returns null

tools.name: makeClassificationSchema
tools.description: Creates a validation schema for intent classification results, defining the structure for classified customer intents with confidence scores. Supports two taxonomy versions (v1 and v2).
preconditions: INTENT_VALUES_V1 and INTENT_VALUES_V2 constants must be defined
postconditions: Schema object is returned that can validate intent classification results

tools.name: classifyByLLM
tools.description: Performs intent classification using a Large Language Model as a fallback when keyword matching fails. Uses structured output with primary and fallback models.
preconditions: Intent descriptions must be defined for the specified version
postconditions: Intent classification result is returned with confidence score
side_effects: Makes API calls to LLM providers

tools.name: routerNode
tools.description: Routes incoming WhatsApp messages by classifying intent. Attempts fast keyword matching first, falls back to LLM classification if no match. This is the entry point for message classification.
postconditions: State.intent field is populated with classified intent
Classification method (keyword or LLM) is recorded
side_effects: May trigger LLM API calls if keyword matching fails

tools.name: statusNode
tools.description: Handles status inquiry intents by executing tools to retrieve order data and formatting responses using LLM with Anthropic as primary and GPT as fallback.
postconditions: Response text is generated with order status information
Tools are executed to fetch order data
side_effects: Executes database queries for order information
Makes LLM API calls for response formatting

tools.name: supportNode
tools.description: Handles support-related intents including goodbye messages and customer support inquiries. Provides fast-path for goodbye intent and routes to appropriate support channels.
postconditions: Response text is prepared for customer
Support routing information is provided if needed

tools.name: warrantyAnswerNode
tools.description: Generates responses for warranty-related inquiries. Checks for active orders and provides appropriate warranty information or prompts for order details if none found.
postconditions: Response text is generated appropriate to warranty inquiry and order status

tools.name: baseState
tools.description: Creates a base/default WhatsApp conversation state object for testing or initialization with mock customer and session data.
postconditions: Mock state object is returned

tools.name: so
tools.description: Creates a mock service order object for testing purposes with default or overridden values.
postconditions: Mock service order object is returned

tools.name: assertNoHedgeWords
tools.description: Test assertion utility that verifies response text does not contain hedging words (e.g., 'maybe', 'possibly', 'might') to ensure confident customer communications.
postconditions: Test assertion completes

tools.name: escalateDetectedEvent
tools.description: Records and escalates detected events (e.g., customer frustration, urgent issues) to the escalations table. Includes deduplication to prevent multiple escalations for the same conversation and event type.
postconditions: Escalation event is recorded in database if not already present
Interaction is logged
side_effects: Writes to escalations table in database
May trigger notifications or workflows for human review

tools.name: EventDetector
tools.description: Interface definition for event detection plugins that analyze conversation context to identify specific events (like address changes, order confirmations, payment receipts). Each detector examines a message and returns a detected event if its pattern matches, otherwise null.
preconditions: EventDetectionContext must be provided with valid message data
postconditions: Returns structured event data if detection criteria met
No state changes - pure detection logic
side_effects: None - read-only interface for event detection

tools.name: verifyDetectedEvents
tools.description: Uses an LLM (GPT-4o-mini) to verify and filter candidate events detected by EventDetector implementations. Acts as a secondary validation layer to confirm or suppress false positives. Designed to fail-open (allow events through on error).
preconditions: OPENAI_MODEL environment variable should be set (defaults to gpt-4o-mini)
Candidate events must be valid DetectedEvent objects
postconditions: Returns verified events that survived LLM validation
Runs synchronously inline during customer conversation turn
side_effects: Sends data to external OpenAI API
Creates tracked LLM call for monitoring

tools.name: address
tools.description: Detects when a user provides or requests to change their address in a text message. Uses regex patterns to identify address-related content and determines if it's an address change request.
postconditions: Returns DetectedEvent if address pattern matches
Identifies whether it's an address change vs. new address

tools.name: order_received
tools.description: Detects when a user confirms they have received their order. Uses positive and negative regex patterns to identify order receipt confirmations while filtering out negations.
preconditions: Message must not match negative patterns (e.g., 'have not received')
postconditions: Returns DetectedEvent with order confirmation details if positive pattern matches

tools.name: payment_receipt
tools.description: Detects when a user uploads a payment receipt as an image or document. Analyzes media attachments to identify payment/receipt content.
preconditions: Message type must be 'image' or 'document' (not text)
Message content (media reference) must be present
postconditions: Returns DetectedEvent with payment receipt metadata if receipt patterns detected in media
side_effects: None - read-only detection, though may process/analyze uploaded media

prompts.name: ROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT
prompts.content:
`You are an intent classifier for TechRepair Polanco Service Center's WhatsApp support.

Your job is to classify customer messages into one of these intents:
{intent_descriptions}

Classification rules:
1. Focus on the customer's PRIMARY intent
2. Look for keywords but also understand context
3. If unsure between two intents, choose the more specific one
4. Messages in Spanish should be classified the same as English equivalents
5. Consider the conversation history for context
6. Escalation signals: frustration keywords ("esto es inaceptable", "quiero hablar con alguien"), repeated issues (same complaint 3+ times), deadline mentions ("ya llevan X días"), threats ("voy a poner queja", "los voy a reportar")
7. When classifying as ESCALATION, preserve the exact trigger phrase in your reasoning
8. Media messages arrive already converted to text with prefixes like "[Nota de voz]:", "[Imagen]:", or "[Video]:" — classify based on the text that follows the prefix as if the customer had typed it. If the message is a placeholder ("[Nota de voz recibida — no se pudo procesar]", "[Imagen recibida — no se pudo procesar]", or "[Video recibido — no se pudo procesar]"), classify based on conversation history context (the customer needs help but we can't read the file yet)

Respond with ONLY the intent name, nothing else.`

prompts.name: ROUTER_USER_PROMPT
STATUS_SYSTEM_PROMPT
prompts.content:
`Eres el asistente de seguimiento de órdenes del Centro de Servicio TechRepair Polanco.
You are the order tracking assistant for TechRepair Polanco Service Center.

Tu especialidad es informar a los clientes sobre el estado de sus reparaciones.
Your specialty is informing customers about the status of their repairs.

IMPORTANTE: Las preguntas de costo/cotización las maneja otro nodo (pricing_answer) con datos de GSPN. Si el cliente pregunta por precio, responde con base en los datos de la orden solamente; NO inventes ni cites un monto que no venga en los resultados de las herramientas.

Reglas / Rules:
1. Presenta la información de forma clara y organizada
2. Si el cliente tiene múltiples órdenes, resume cada una
3. Responde en el mismo idioma del cliente
4. Máximo {max_length} caracteres
5. NUNCA menciones "sustitución", "reemplazo" o "cambio de equipo" como opción. Solo menciona reparación. Los clientes usan estas palabras para exigir equipos nuevos
6. NUNCA inventes tiempos estimados de reparación o entrega. Solo reporta datos que existan en los resultados de las herramientas
7. NUNCA determines garantía por tu cuenta. Solo reporta lo que dice el sistema (warranty_type)
8. SERVICIO DOOR-TO-DOOR (D2D): Si la orden tiene service_type = "d2d", NUNCA menciones recoger, pasar al centro, ni cualquier instrucción que implique que el cliente debe ir a un lugar. El equipo será ENTREGADO en su domicilio. Solo informa que será enviado a la dirección registrada
9. NUNCA inventes ni uses números de teléfono. El ÚNICO número de contacto válido es {support_phone}. Cualquier otro número es INCORRECTO
10. NUNCA inventes datos que no estén en los resultados de herramientas: números de guía, fechas de entrega, nombres de paqueterías, horarios de entrega, ni cualquier dato logístico
11. Si el cliente proporciona un número de orden diferente al que tienes registrado y no se encuentra en el sistema, NO insistas en la orden vinculada. Reconoce que no encontraste su orden y sugiere verificar

prompts.name: STATUS_USER_PROMPT
SUPPORT_SYSTEM_PROMPT
prompts.content:
`Eres el asistente virtual del Centro de Servicio TechRepair Polanco en la Ciudad de México.
You are the virtual assistant for TechRepair Polanco Service Center in Mexico City.

Tu rol es ayudar a los clientes con:
- Consultas sobre reparaciones de dispositivos TechRepair
- Información sobre servicios disponibles
- Horarios y ubicación del centro de servicio
- Resolución de dudas generales

Your role is to help customers with:
- Inquiries about TechRepair device repairs
- Information about available services
- Service center hours and location
- General question resolution

Información del Centro de Servicio / Service Center Information:
- Nombre: {business_name}
- Dirección: {business_address}
- Horario: {business_hours}
- Teléfono de atención (consulta de estado por teléfono): {support_phone}
- Teléfono directo de la tienda (hablar con una persona): {store_phone}
- Correo: {business_email}

Reglas de respuesta / Response rules:
1. Responde en el idioma del cliente (español o inglés)
2. Sé amigable, profesional y conciso
3. Si no estás seguro de una respuesta, recomienda contactar directamente al centro
4. IMPORTANTE: Tu respuesta DEBE ser menor a {max_length} caracteres. Sé directo y conciso. No repitas información que el cliente ya tiene. Evita saludos largos o despedidas innecesarias
5. Usa formato WhatsApp cuando sea útil (negritas con *texto*, listas con -)
6. Si el cliente está frustrado o pide hablar con un humano, registra EXACTAMENTE sus palabras en tu respuesta
7. Si detectas información contradictoria del cliente, anota ambas versiones
8. Al escalar, incluye: motivo específico, cita textual del cliente, nivel de urgencia
9. Si el cliente menciona plazos incumplidos, registra las fechas específicas mencionadas
10. NO resumas quejas en lenguaje genérico — usa las palabras exactas del cliente
11. Cuando el cliente mencione un problema técnico (pantalla rota, no enciende, batería, carga, agua, etc.) sin especificar el modelo EXACTO del dispositivo, PREGUNTA antes de dar

interactions.description: Rule 14 prohibits mentioning replacement/substitution, but Rule 21 requires not inventing pricing data. If customer asks about replacement costs and system shows no data, these rules could create tension about what to communicate.
Both rules prohibit inventing data - R15 for repair times, R19 for logistics data. They work together to ensure only verified information is shared.
Both require preserving exact customer words during escalation. R7 for trigger phrases, R28 for escalation context including quotes.
R26 requires recording contradictory information, R27 requires noting missed deadlines. Both support detailed escalation documentation.
Both enforce character limits - R13 as simple constraint, R24 with additional instructions about conciseness and avoiding repetition.
R17 handles D2D service prohibition of pickup instructions, R19 prohibits inventing logistics data. Together they ensure accurate D2D communication.
R6 defines escalation triggers, R28 specifies what to include when escalating. They work sequentially in the escalation workflow.
R31 requires including order cards textually without modification, R15 prohibits inventing repair times. Both enforce data accuracy from tools.
R20 handles order lookup failures, R23 provides fallback to recommend direct contact when uncertain. Both guide handling missing information.
R3 is fallback for intent classification uncertainty, R23 is fallback for answer uncertainty. Both provide escalation paths when AI lacks confidence.

R29 prohibits generic summaries of complaints (use exact words), while R30 requires asking questions when device model missing. For complaint escalations about unspecified devices, tension exists between preserving exact words vs. gathering more info.
R35 specifies event verification considering negations and sarcasm, R34 gives specific example for order_received. They work together in event detection logic.
R18 prohibits inventing phone numbers, R21 prohibits inventing pricing data. Both are specific instances of the broader 'don't fabricate data' principle.
R8 requires classifying media messages based on context/history, R5 requires considering conversation history. They ensure context-aware classification.
Both require language matching - R12 for status responses, R4 for intent classification. Ensures consistent language throughout interaction.

nodes.name: getActiveOrders
nodes.description:
Get active orders from assembled context.

Returns a deterministically sorted copy (svc_order_no DESC) so nodes that
pick `orders[0]` always resolve to the same SO across calls. TechRepair SO
numbers are monotonically increasing, so DESC approximates "newest first"
— the right default when a customer with multiple active SOs asks a
question without naming one.

Load-bearing for warranty_answer and pricing_answer, both of which use
`orders[0]` as the single-SO case.

nodes.name: parseCorrections
nodes.description:
Extract all `[CORRECT:...]` markers from the LLM's response text,
validate each, and return the parsed-and-validated corrections plus
the text with the markers stripped out.

Validation failures are collected, not thrown — the LLM should never
crash the response just because it formatted a marker wrong.

nodes.name: applyCorrections
nodes.description:
Persist applied corrections. Updates `customer_memory` for whitelisted
fields and appends one `interaction_history` row per correction with
`metadata.source='human_correction'` so audit can show the chain
"customer said X → agent emitted marker → DB updated to Y".

Non-throwing: a DB hiccup must not break the customer's reply. Errors
are logged and the caller proceeds. The reply has already been generated.

nodes.name: truncateResponse
nodes.description:
Truncate response to WhatsApp character limit.

Tries to break at a sentence boundary if possible.

nodes.name: buildEscalationResponse
nodes.description:
Build escalation response text — the message the customer sees when
the bot escalates without a typed `escalationReasonOverride`.

Wording principles (W1 Task 8):
  - Mexican Spanish tuteo (never voseo, never usted).
  - No "transfer" / "we'll contact you" framing — WhatsApp is async
    in the same chat thread; the human just takes over silently via
    `humanTakenOverNode`. Promising a transfer or a callback creates
    false expectations.
  - No timing promises ("enseguida", "en un momento") — escalation
    latency depends on staff availability, not the bot.
  - When an active order is in scope, ground the message with the
    order number to confirm the bot heard the customer correctly and
    to disambiguate when the customer has multiple orders.

The `reason` parameter is preserved for callers that still pass it
(fully unused in the user-facing text — leaking internal slugs to
customers was a long-standing bug).

nodes.name: resolveTypedReason
nodes.description:
Resolve the typed EscalationReason for this escalation, if any: an explicit
override slug wins, else the frustration-intent mapping. Returns undefined
when neither applies (caller falls back to the legacy generic bounce).

nodes.name: buildHandoffContext
nodes.description:
Derive the handoff context from graph state. Register defaults to
`default_formal` until D12's register_lock lands; the customer name is
the first token of the stored name (if any) and svcOrderNo is the first
active order's number. The store line is attached so the human-frustration
handoffs can offer a direct call (renderHandoff ignores it otherwise).

nodes.name: buildWaitTimeNotice
nodes.description: Build wait time notice if the session window is closing.

nodes.name: escalationNode
nodes.description:
Escalation node — marks the conversation as escalated.

Resolution order for the customer-facing handoff text:
  1. If state.responseText is already set (node did its own render via
     paymentPendingEscalation / renderHandoff), keep it verbatim.
  2. Else if we can resolve a typed EscalationReason — from the override
     slug, or by mapping a frustration intent (complaint / explicit-human)
     to its reason — emit the D13 renderHandoff copy with state-derived ctx.
     For the human-frustration cluster this also appends the direct store
     line so the customer reaches a person, not the AI line.
  3. Else fall back to the legacy generic bounce (buildEscalationResponse).

Persisted `escalation_reason` is the enum slug when we have one (so
dashboard queue filters work), else the free-text string.
